oneLiner: AI-native neocloud converting a $46B-plus Microsoft and Meta backlog into revenue growing 454%, now part-funding its $20-25B capex bet with $5.75B of fresh converts -- and paying for it in dilution and an 18% post-earnings round trip.
thesis: The backlog is anchored by two of the largest AI buyers on earth. Microsoft signed a five-year $17.4B dedicated-capacity contract (September 2025, expandable to $19.4B) served from a new Vineland, New Jersey site. Meta grew from a $3B five-year deal (December 2025) to a $12B commitment plus a $15B option (May 2026), taking potential backlog above $46B.

Growth is hyperscaler-fast and, unusually for a neocloud, EBITDA-positive. Q2 2026 (reported August 12, 2026) revenue rose 454% YoY to $582.3M with AI Cloud up 514%, and adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $236M, a 41% margin.

The balance sheet plus strategic stakes give funding options peers lack, now topped up with converts. Nebius held roughly $9.3B of cash at Q2 2026, closed a $5.75B convertible senior notes offering on Aug 24, 2026, and owns stakes in ClickHouse (~28%), Avride (~83%), Toloka and TripleTen, an estimated $7-8B of monetizable value versus CoreWeave's $50.8B of total liabilities.

Management is running a power land-grab. On the August 12, 2026 call, the year-end contracted power target was raised to 5 GW, with four new AI cloud deals averaging more than $1B of total contract value each at $20-25M annual contract value per megawatt.

Execution is the whole story, and financing is no longer free. The 2026 capex guide of $20-25B (raised from $16-20B in May 2026) is several times the cash on hand; the August financings -- an $800M convert-for-equity swap (15.8M shares, ~5.5% dilution per Reuters) followed by the $5.75B convert raise -- closed part of the gap but knocked roughly 18% off the stock in under two weeks.

latestProse: Nebius reported Q2 2026 on August 12: revenue of $582.3 million, up 454% year over year with AI Cloud up 514%, and adjusted EBITDA swinging positive to $236 million, a 41% margin. Adjusted EPS of -$0.12 beat the -$0.69 consensus by a wide margin, annualized run-rate revenue hit $3.0 billion, and management closed four new AI cloud contracts averaging more than $1 billion of total value each. Shares surged roughly 34% on the print to ~$254 intraday -- then gave essentially all of it back: an $800M convert-for-equity swap (~5.5% dilution), a $5B convertible offering priced Aug 19 (closed Aug 24 at $5.75B, with convert buyers shorting the stock to hedge), and Friday reports of an IPO by Nvidia-backed rival Nscale took the stock down about 18% to ~$209 by Aug 24. The disclosure that matters most: the year-end contracted power target was raised to 5 gigawatts while capex ran $5.7 billion in the quarter alone -- Nebius is selling 2027-2028 capacity faster than it can build or finance it, and August showed what the financing costs.
guidanceProse: Management reaffirmed 2026 guidance on August 12, 2026: revenue of $3.0-3.4 billion, an adjusted EBITDA margin near 40%, capex of $20-25 billion (raised from $16-20 billion in May 2026), and an annualized run-rate revenue exit of $7-9 billion. The central debate is the bridge from the $3.0 billion Q2 run-rate to that exit, which requires Vineland and other sites to energize on schedule in H2. The funding debate moved in August: roughly $9.3 billion of quarter-end cash was joined by $5.75 billion of convertible notes (closed Aug 24) and an $800 million convert-for-equity swap, on top of customer prepayments, a $775 million asset-backed facility and stake monetizations -- still short of a $20-25 billion capex bill, so more debt or dilution into 2027 remains the base case.

segments: AI Cloud (core): GPU infrastructure and AI cloud platform, up 514% YoY in Q2 2026; the Microsoft and Meta dedicated-capacity contracts sit here, served from New Jersey, Finland, UK and Israel data centers
Software and inference layer: Token Factory plus the 2026 acquisitions (Tavily, Eigen AI, Clarifai) aimed at higher-margin, usage-based revenue on top of raw compute

Strategic stakes: ClickHouse (~28% diluted, ~$15B round reported early 2026), Avride (~83% after the Uber-led round, ~$2.7-2.8B post-money), Toloka (majority economic interest) and TripleTen -- an estimated $7-8B of monetizable value
competitive: CoreWeave (CRWV): the levered mirror image. CRWV reported Q2 2026 revenue of ~$2.58B on August 11, 2026 with a ~$104B backlog, but carries ~$50.8B of total liabilities against $2.2B cash; Nebius runs the same land-grab with ~$9.3B cash and far less leverage
Microsoft (MSFT): simultaneously Nebius's largest customer ($17.4B contract) and a hyperscaler that could in-source capacity once its own buildout catches up -- the definitive frenemy risk
Oracle (ORCL): OCI is the aggressive incumbent bidder for the same multi-GW AI deals, with a balance sheet Nebius cannot match
IREN (IREN): power-first bitcoin-miner-turned-neocloud competing on cheap energy for the next wave of GPU capacity

Nscale: London-based, Nvidia-backed neocloud reportedly targeting a U.S. IPO of up to $3B as early as September 2026, telling investors it has ~$51B of contracted revenue -- fresh public-market supply chasing the same multi-GW deals (per Bloomberg/TipRanks, Aug 2026)
Hyperscaler internal buildouts (MSFT, META, GOOGL) are the structural ceiling: every megawatt they self-build in 2027-2028 is a megawatt Nebius does not rent
moat: Honestly, the moat is thin and time-based rather than structural: contracted power, energized sites and delivery speed during a supply-constrained window, plus a Yandex-heritage engineering team that runs full-stack software on its own hardware. Five-year take-or-pay contracts with Microsoft and Meta provide revenue lock-in, but GPUs depreciate fast and customers are also competitors. If AI compute stays scarce through 2028, the head start compounds; if supply normalizes, this is a capital-intensive rental business.
risks: Funding gap and dilution: $20-25B of 2026 capex against roughly $9.3B quarter-end cash plus $5.75B of new converts; the August financings cost ~5.5% dilution (the $800M swap) plus convert-arb short pressure, and still leave a hole implying more debt or equity into 2027
Customer concentration: Microsoft and Meta represent the large majority of the $46B-plus potential backlog; either pausing deployments would gut the growth story
GPU depreciation and obsolescence: five-year contracts ride on silicon that may be economically obsolete in three; accounting lives versus real lives is the sector's open question
Execution: Vineland NJ energization, transformer and power supply chains, and the jump from ~$3.0B to $7-9B run-rate in two quarters leave no room for slippage
Pricing: $20-25M ACV per MW compresses if CoreWeave, Oracle, IREN and hyperscaler self-build flood 2027 supply
Governance and structure: founder voting control, a Russia-origin corporate history, and a stake portfolio whose sum-of-parts value is hard to realize on demand
catalysts: Q3 2026 earnings, expected early-to-mid November 2026 (date unconfirmed): first read on the H2 ramp toward the $7-9B ARR exit
Vineland, New Jersey deliveries to Microsoft ramping through H2 2026
Year-end 2026 checkpoint: 5 GW contracted power target and the $7-9B ARR exit, reported with Q4 results expected February 2027
Potential ClickHouse IPO or further stake monetization, 2026-2027 (timing unverified)
New multi-GW customer announcements; management flagged additional landmark-deal pipeline on the August 12, 2026 call
pricedIn: At about $209 on August 24, 2026 (down ~18% from the ~$254 post-earnings peak), Nebius carries a market cap near $57 billion -- roughly 18x the midpoint of 2026 revenue guidance and about 7x the midpoint of the $7-9 billion year-end ARR exit target. Strip out an estimated $7-8 billion of strategic stakes and net cash, and the core AI cloud trades somewhat cheaper. The price implies the ARR exit is hit, capex converts to contracted revenue at $20-25 million per megawatt, and Microsoft and Meta keep deploying into 2028. August added a new term to the debate: the growth is real (sell-side average target ~$273, Goldman street-high $328 on Aug 25), but each capacity tranche is now visibly paid for in converts, dilution and hedging flow -- and Nscale's planned IPO prices the competing supply.

scenarios.bear: The buildout slips and the AI capex cycle cools into 2027. Vineland energization delays push revenue toward the low end of guidance, the $7-9 billion ARR exit is missed, and follow-on contracts price below $20 million per megawatt as CoreWeave, Oracle, Nscale and hyperscaler self-build flood supply. Closing the remaining capex funding gap requires further dilutive equity or expensive debt on top of August's $5.75B converts. Revenue still compounds around 25%, but the exit multiple compresses toward 3x sales and the stock rerates far below today's $57 billion.
scenarios.base: Nebius hits the 2026 guide, exits near the low end of the $7-9 billion ARR target, and Microsoft and Meta deployments ramp through 2027 as contracted. Revenue compounds around 40% for several years, adjusted EBITDA margins hold near 40%, and free cash flow turns positive around 2028-2029 as the capex wave crests. Stake monetizations, led by ClickHouse, plus the August converts cover most of the funding gap. A 4-5x exit revenue multiple roughly supports today's price with modest annual upside.
scenarios.bull: Demand keeps outrunning supply. The 5 gigawatt contracted power book converts at $20-25 million ACV per megawatt, ARR exits 2026 above $9 billion, and 2027 guidance shocks upward. Token Factory, Tavily and Clarifai lift margins above pure-infrastructure peers, ClickHouse lists well above its reported $15 billion mark, and Nebius becomes the fourth Western AI cloud at scale. Revenue compounds above 55%, the multiple holds near 6x sales, and the stock is a multi-bagger from $57 billion.

valPresets.note: Revenue mode: the $20-25B 2026 capex program keeps free cash flow deeply negative despite a 41% adjusted EBITDA margin, so revenue trajectory and exit multiple carry the valuation. Base assumes the FY26 guide is met and ARR converts; margins reflect steady-state FCF after the buildout crests, not current burn.
